description.narrative:
Project Outcome:
i) Stakeholders Effects Increase access to finance for MSMEs and women-owned enterprises: Perus credit market remains shallow, with credit to GDP at about 45%. Access to finance is more limited for smaller enterprises, and the formal MSME finance gap is estimated at US$10 billion, or 4.7% of GDP. IFCs investment will support Vinci Compass Peru in expanding financing for corporations, including women-owned enterprises. Women-led MSMEs are more likely to be credit constrained than men-led MSMEs (27.0% vs. 16.7%), despite lower past-due loan ratios, which shows they remain underserved.
The Project will help create jobs by providing MSMEs with working capital to grow. MSMEs account for 31% of GDP and nearly 60% of employment in Peru. By improving access to finance, the Project will support growth, competitiveness, and job preservation.
Market Creation Outcome:
ii) Competitiveness: The Project will support private investment funds in Peru as an alternative source of financing alongside banks, in a concentrated market where banks and CMACs dominate MSME lending. This is particularly relevant for MSMEs, which still rely heavily on supplier credit and short-term bank lines. By supporting factoring and reverse factoring, the Project will help broaden access to working capital, improve market contestability, and strengthen supply chains by allowing suppliers to convert receivables into immediate liquidity. IFCs participation and advisory support will also help mobilize new investors into private debt and strengthen the Funds capacity to identify and serve more enterprises, including women-owned enterprises, while promoting more diversified financing channels for Peruvian corporates.

The proposed investment consists of up to US$40 million (equivalent in PEN) or up to 20% of the total commitments in Compass Fondo de Inversion Adelanto de Efectivo (Compass FAE or the Fund), an unlisted, closed-ended, PEN-denominated trade receivables investment fund in Peru, for a period of up to 8 years. With IFCs anchor participation, a mobilization ratio of at least 1:1 is expected (the Project). The Project will build on Word Bank Group (WBG) engagements to develop the factoring and reverse factoring as an alternative financial intermediation channel in Peru and support micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) by providing financing through factoring and reverse factoring.
